observations.seen: The Forest frames have a warm sun, and the 3/4 key light gives readable form on the coral platforms. The Clouds and Palace frames are flat and washed out, with almost no directional modeling on the floors.
Pip casts a soft contact shadow. The tree shadows on the grass in frame 1 are blurry and low-resolution. In the Palace frame, the platforms are barely grounded by any shadow.
The palace towers show strong chrome reflections that clash with the matte, untextured floors. Elsewhere there is little environment response and the scene reads as mostly flat diffuse.
The levels are box platforms floating in a void. The Clouds level is a bare brown slab with a windmill and a pagoda placed far away. The Palace has an empty white backdrop with no ground context.
Only faint distance haze appears in the Forest frames. The Clouds sky is a hazy backdrop but no fog layering ties it to the platforms. The Palace has no atmosphere at all.
Platforms use plain untextured coral, white, tan and brown materials. The Pip character and the gate are richly detailed, which creates a large fidelity mismatch.

There are mixed art styles throughout. Pip is a polished stylized model, the NPC is a blocky voxel humanoid, the drones are hard-surface sci-fi, and the trees are low-poly cones. Together they read as a kitbash.
In frame 1 the NPC block clips into Pip and fills the center of the shot. Frames 3 and 4 have large empty floor areas in the lower half while the goal sits small and distant.
The chase cam behind Pip frames the route forward with a reasonable FOV and Pip at roughly 15-20% of the frame. In frame 1 it clips through the NPC and trees.
There is mild bloom in the Forest frames. The Clouds and Palace frames look overexposed and low-contrast, with no grading consistency between levels.
Pip's run and idle poses read with personality. A static frame cannot judge timing, but the frame 1 overlap suggests collision and penetration issues.
The HUD has clean, readable pills, a useful objective banner and a controls strip. However, the debug-style top nav bar takes up chrome space.
